item.title: ‘You can’t hide forever’: Calls mount for CLP MLA to publicly explain bullying allegations
item.description: CLP backbencher Tanzil Rahman needs to publicly explain the bullying allegations that were levelled against him by two female parliamentary staffers, independent MLAs and the Opposition have said, which follows the Chief Minister's attempts to keep the "sensitive HR matter" secret, which she claimed was "out of respect for all parties", despite the matter already being resolved.

item.title: Seven arrested over brutal baseball bat and scooter attack on teen girl
item.description: Seven girls and women have been arrested in Alice Springs for allegedly bashing a 16-year-old female last Friday which NT Police did not make public until today, while a video of the brutal attack shows the victim being being hit in the head with a scooter, bashed with a metal baseball bat, her head kicked and stomped on, and her assailants trying to smash her head into a bitumen road. Police have also alleged the group "forcibly removed her clothes" following the beating.

item.title: Bowman’s ‘head must roll’ over CDU TAFE stuff-up, federal inquiry held: MLA
item.description: A federal inquiry into Charles Darwin University's governance practices and general "competency" should be ordered immediately and vice-chancellor Scott Bowman's "head must roll", an independent MLA has said, in the wake of revelations nearly 400 CDU TAFE students and others were graduated without proper qualifications.

item.title: NT Criminal Court list – with charges – Feb 23
item.description: The 247 names facing criminal courts in the Northern Territory for Monday, February 23, 2026. This list includes all the charges.

item.title: Jake Danby’s home detention order extended to two years on appeal
item.description: Jake Danby, the step-nephew of Attorney-General Marie-Clare Boothby, who bragged to friends and family about killing an Aboriginal man in a hit-and-run, had his sentence increased on Friday to two years home detention following an appeal of the original sentence.

item.title: Minister demands answers from national skills regulator over CDU TAFE scandal
item.description: Education and Training Minister Jo Hersey has called on the Australian Skills Quality Authority to explain how the national regulator re-registered Charles Darwin University's TAFE program last September without picking up on the massive accreditation failures that has now led to hundreds of students needing to resit their qualifications, amid continued calls for Scott Bowman's resignation.

item.title: Opinion: Why are there two medical schools in Darwin and why do taxpayers have to pay for both?
item.description: The Northern Territory now has two medical schools, but with an existing, successful partnership already in place, Dr Don Fuller argues that the new Charles Darwin University-Menzies program is an expensive exercise in duplication and may create an unstated incentive to enrol more full-fee paying international students rather that training Territorians, particularly Indigenous Territorians.

item.title: Territory doctors reject government’s pay offer
item.description: NT public doctors have rejected a four-year pay offer from the Finocchiaro Government which was less than the increase given to public servant generally and police officers, with 82 per cent of those who voted, voting against it, the Australian Salaried Medical Officers' Federation has said.

item.title: Calls for Police Commissioner to explain why executive team is under investigation by the AFP
item.description: Territory police officers want to know why the entire NT Police top brass is currently under investigation by the Australian Federal Police, the union representing the cops has said, while questions about perceived conflicts of interest in the investigation have been ignored by all involved.

item.title: Bobo to go-go: Scott Bowman out as CDU vice-chancellor amid growing scandal
item.description: Scott Bowman's role as vice-chancellor and president of Charles Darwin University has ended, the university has confirmed, amid the growing accreditation scandal that has affected hundreds of TAFE students, Territory businesses and others, with the full scope of the damage still being assessed.
